study/hypothesis: III-V and II-VI compounds have a direct gap more often than the rest, which is why light emitters are made of them and not of silicon.
study/name: Are III-V and II-VI semiconductors more often direct-gap?
study/question: Among stable elements and binary compounds with a band gap, is the share with a direct gap higher for III-V and II-VI compounds than for the rest (group IV elements, IV-IV, I-VII, IV-VI and other compounds)?
